advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit assertion that pins the no-op guard directly (e.g. capture the `entry` object identity or a mutation counter and assert set_baseline with an equal value does NOT re-touch the entry), so the test flips if the `entry.get("baseline") == baseline: return` branch is removed.
evidence: Guard under test at src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py:463-466: `baseline = {k: fields.get(k) ...}` / `if entry.get("baseline") == baseline: return` / `entry["baseline"] = baseline`

save() is deterministic: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py:306 `json.dump(self._data, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)` — an equal dict re-assigned serializes identically with or without the early-return
set_baseline no longer stamps a timestamp (baseline_advanced_at removed in the diff), so nothing in the second set_baseline+save can differ regardless of the guard
bind_confirm (the only `_now_iso` caller here) is invoked at test line 65, BEFORE the monkeypatch at line 67, so it uses the real clock — the iterator is never advanced
advisory.finding: The unit test `test_unchanged_baseline_keeps_serialized_bytes_identical` does not gate the new no-op guard (`if entry.get("baseline") == baseline: return`) it is meant to protect: with `baseline_advanced_at` removed and `save()` serializing deterministically (`json.dump(..., sort_keys=True)`), re-assigning an equal baseline dict already yields byte-identical output, so the assertion `read_bytes() == first_bytes` passes even if the guard is deleted. It only detects the timestamp removal, not the guard.
merged_from: The `_now_iso` monkeypatch in `test_unchanged_baseline_keeps_serialized_bytes_identical` and `test_seed_baselines_unchanged_keeps_serialized_bytes_identical` is inert: `set_baseline` (and `seed_baselines_from_snapshot`, which delegates to it) no longer calls `_now_iso` after the diff, and `bind_confirm` (which does call it) runs before the patch is installed. The two-value timestamp iterator is never consumed, giving a false impression that the test defends against a timestamp rewrite that can no longer occur.
scenarios: A refactor that drops the `entry.get("baseline") == baseline` early-return would leave this test green, hiding loss of the intended no-op semantics.
